source.title: How Pruning Reshapes Features: Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Weight-Pruned Language Models
source.authors: Hector Borobia; Elies Seguí-Mas; Guillermina Tormo-Carbó

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results on whether SAE features are stable across random seeds, directly challenging the version that treats SAE features as stable, canonical units. It also measures SAE reconstruction on pruned LLMs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports additional pruning, perplexity, and firing-rate findings. The feature-survival and firing-rate results do not directly test the specified superposition, capacity, or one-dimensional-feature versions; the distinct rare-versus-frequent survival finding is recorded under fits_no_version. Values used for the logistic predictor are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: RQ1 trains 3–5 TopK SAEs per condition with different seeds and reports cross-seed MNN match rates of 1.1–3.9% at τ=0.7 (Section 4.2, Figure 1). This bears directly on V5's claim that dictionary features are stable, canonical units. The other results (pruned-model transfer, dense→pruned survival, firing-rate fragility, ablation KL) concern how pruning changes SAE dictionaries, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors say population-level statistics and the response to pruning are stable across seeds, even though individual features are not reproducible. They also frame the low seed MNN as expected for large TopK dictionaries, which admit many equivalent decompositions.
record.recipe_differences: This study analyzes SAE features in weight-pruned LLMs; it does not apply the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Pruning method and sparsity change feature survival and SAE reconstruction; the paper reports better preservation with Wanda than magnitude pruning.

fits_no_version.finding: Dense-trained official SAEs reconstruct Wanda-pruned activations nearly as well as dense ones (Gemma 3 FVU 0.024 vs 0.011 at 50%), but transfer worse to magnitude-pruned activations (Gemma 2 0.533 at 50%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries trained on a dense LLM transfer to activation-aware pruned versions of it, but not as well to magnitude-pruned versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Dense→pruned SAE feature survival falls with sparsity and is higher under Wanda than magnitude pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wanda pruning preserves more SAE-matched feature directions than magnitude pruning at matched sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: Rare SAE features survive pruning better than frequent ones (ρ ≤ −0.8 in 15 of 17 conditions; Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In pruned LLMs, lower-firing-rate SAE features are more likely to retain their decoder direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Robust and fragile features have nearly identical single-ablation KL (≤1.2% difference; Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric survival of SAE features under pruning does not predict their causal importance.

record.problems: All tested models are 1–2B parameters; activation extraction uses context length 256; two Gemma 3 layer-18 runs failed from float16 overflow; the study uses one-shot pruning without fine-tuning; and low seed-to-seed MNN means the specific robust and fragile features may depend on seed choice. The paper reports some outcomes in figures without full numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were extracted from figure-only plots. The full firing-rate-by-quintile survival table (Table 3) and feature-ablation KL results (Table 4) were not included because the specified versions do not name those outcomes; the rare-versus-frequent survival result is summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No toy models or geometry of superposition are studied.
No test of capacity competition or of polysemanticity.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.

The study does not test whether dense LLMs distribute features across neurons or contain sparse SAE-recoverable features. Its own SAEs' dense FVU (~0.36–0.41) is reported only as a training-quality check.
Completeness and canonicity across dictionary sizes, architectures and corpora are not tested. Only seed-to-seed reproducibility (and pruning-induced change) is tested.

missing.what: Overall cross-seed MNN range of 1.1–3.9% across all conditions (mean 2.8%), including Gemma 2 2B seed stability, which appears only in Figure 1

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 links are removed. The transfer rows test whether SAEs remain valid after compression, not whether dense LLMs contain SAE-recoverable sparse features, so the reader's V4 supports and limits_scope labels are dropped. For V5, the low cross-seed match is specific to TopK SAEs with 8× expansion and k=64, at τ=0.7 with the conservative MNN metric; the one-way match rate would likely be higher. The record's tranche_reason and per-version status, which still list V4 as tested, should be updated to match.

versions.untested_parts: Whether toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions store overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited representational capacity or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study measures SAE reconstruction and reuse on pruned LLMs, not whether features are distributed across neurons or whether SAE features are independently verified as the model's underlying features.
Seed-to-seed matching is tested, but completeness, stability across methods and corpora, and canonical status of SAE features are not established.
Whether underlying model features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
